question: The population of a city increases 5% annually in compounded manner (yearly compounding). The present population of this city is 93051. The population of this city 2 years ago was:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Multiplying factor for a 5% increase = 100% + 5% = 105% = 21/20.

For 2 years, the population becomes (21/20)² of the original.

Population 2 years ago = Present Population × (20/21)²

⇒ Population 2 years ago = 93051 × (400/441)

⇒ Population = 211 × 400 = 84400

**∴ The correct answer is 84400.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Present population of the city (A) = 93051

Annual increase rate (R) = 5%

Time period (n) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

A = P(1 + R/100)ⁿ

Where A is the final population and P is the initial population.
